answer.rationale: Expiry in 14 days on a non-auto-renewing primary, with the line at 94% and no buffer, makes continuity the binding constraint on TCO. memory_c1 is the only inherited path that explicitly avoided migration and delivery interruption. Incumbent already refused a price reopen, so negotiate_terms is unlikely to land an 18% cut in time. Deferral (memory_c5) was for non-critical month-to-month service and would open a supply gap here. Switch or second-source could cut unit cost (memory_c2/c3) but introduce onboarding/migration risk we cannot absorb. Renewing the incumbent is the only one-decision move that does not increase delivery risk; the spend mandate is unmet and remains unresolved. Verifying memory_c2 to test whether the historical low-cost switch was actually low-risk enough to reopen that option.
